TECH3_2021-21.exp: PMBOK defines exactly this scope as Project Integration Management: identifying, defining, combining, unifying, and coordinating the processes and activities across all Process Groups.

TECH3_2021-22.exp: PMBOK states integration's nature is captured by the characteristics of unification, consolidation, communication, and interrelationship; 'review' is not one of the four named characteristics.

TECH3_2021-23.exp: Defining, preparing, and organizing the subsidiary management plans and integrating them into one comprehensive project management plan is precisely the Develop Project Management Plan process.

TECH3_2021-24.exp: The Project Scope Management processes run in order: Plan Scope Management, Collect Requirements, Define Scope, Create WBS, Validate Scope, and Control Scope.

TECH3_2021-25.exp: Define Scope produces the project scope statement plus updates to project documents such as the requirements traceability matrix; the WBS is not created until the later Create WBS process, and the project charter predates Define Scope.

TECH3_2021-26.exp: Create WBS is one of the core processes of the Project Scope Management knowledge area.

TECH3_2021-27.exp: Refusing to informally absorb a suggested addition and instead insisting it be routed through the proper process is the discipline of change control, which channels all scope changes through a formal review rather than ad hoc acceptance.

TECH3_2021-28.exp: Control Scope exists mainly to prevent uncontrolled, unapproved additions to the project's deliverables -- i.e. to prevent scope creep -- not to enable it or to simply block all change.

TECH3_2021-29.exp: PMBOK's Validate Scope inputs are the project management plan, project documents, verified deliverables, and work performance data; the scope baseline is only referenced as a component nested inside the project management plan, not listed as its own standalone input.

TECH3_2021-30.exp: The Scope Management Plan is a subsidiary plan bundled inside the overall Project Management Plan, not a standalone document like the WBS or scope statement.

TECH3_2021-31.exp: Determining, documenting, and managing stakeholder needs and requirements to meet project objectives is the definition of the Collect Requirements process.

TECH3_2021-32.exp: Decomposition is the PMBOK technique for subdividing project scope/work into smaller, more manageable components such as activities; 'deconstruction' is not a PMBOK term.

TECH3_2021-33.exp: A resource calendar documents availability (working days/shifts, duration of availability) of already-identified resources; it cannot specify resources that are 'potentially unidentified', which is the false statement here.

TECH3_2021-34.exp: PMBOK names Crashing (adding resources to shorten duration) and Fast Tracking (doing activities in parallel) as the two schedule-compression techniques.

TECH3_2021-35.exp: Establishing/removing logical dependencies between activities and then updating activity attributes to reflect the change are outputs of the Sequence Activities process.

TECH3_2021-36.exp: Starting 10 days before the predecessor finishes is a Finish-to-Start relationship with a 10-day lead (a negative lag applied to an FS dependency), not a different relationship type like Start-to-Start.

TECH3_2021-37.exp: PMBOK's activity-attributes list explicitly names person responsible, geographic area/location, and leads and lags as attributes; a specific 'time when to perform' is not on that list since actual dates only get fixed later as an output of Develop Schedule.

TECH3_2021-38.exp: Customer-imposed milestones bind everyone delivering the work -- both the project manager accountable for the schedule and the functional managers supplying resources against it -- so both must adhere to them, unlike internally set milestones which can be more flexible.

TECH3_2021-39.exp: Rounding rules, units of measure, and variance thresholds for cost control are exactly the kind of detail specified in the Cost Management Plan.

TECH3_2021-40.exp: All subsidiary management plans, including the Cost Management Plan, are integrated together in the Develop Project Management Plan process.
